# odyssey-014 — new rendering candidates (Odyssey 4.1–112)

New formulas / noun-epithet pairs not yet in `conventions.md`'s house table, chosen with the same
care and kept consistent every time they occur within this part. Same row format as the house table.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Μενελάου κυδαλίμοιο (4.2, 4.16, 4.23, 4.46 — all genitive) | "of Menelaus, glorious" | "of glorious Menelaus" | "renowned" (risks confusion with κλέος-root words), "illustrious", "far-famed" (reserved for τηλεκλυτός) |
| ὀτρηρὸς θεράπων / ὀτρηροὺς θεράποντας (4.23, singular, of Eteoneus; 4.38, plural, of the other servants) | "brisk attendant" / "brisk attendants" | "brisk attendant" / "brisk attendants" | "busy squire", "ready servant", "nimble henchman" — ὀτρηρός is 'quick, prompt, ready for service' |
| ὑψερεφές (of Menelaus's hall, 4.15 μέγα δῶμα, 4.46 δῶμα alone) | "high-roofed" | "high-roofed" | "lofty-roofed", "high-ceilinged", "towering" (too free — the compound is literally 'roofed high') |
| ἐχέφρων Πηνελόπεια (4.111) | "sound-minded Penelope" | "sound-minded Penelope" | "prudent Penelope" (reserved for πεπνυμένος), "circumspect Penelope" (the already-fixed rendering of the distinct epithet περίφρων Πηνελόπεια — kept separate since Homer uses two different φρήν-compounds of her), "wise-hearted" (too close to the δαΐφρων reading already fixed for Odysseus) |

## Judgment calls flagged but NOT added above (each occurs only once in this part, so does not yet
meet the "plainly recurs" bar, but a future drafter meeting them again should look here first)

- **κρείων Ἐτεωνεύς** (4.22): rendered "the lord Eteoneus" — κρείων is the ordinary honorific
  "ruling, lordly" already partly spoken for by κρειόντων → "rulers" in the fixed ὕπατε κρειόντων
  row; here it is used loosely as a title for a chief household steward, not a king, so "lord" was
  chosen rather than "ruler". Worth fixing formally once κρείων recurs of another secondary
  character.
- **τὸν δὲ μέγ’ ὀχθήσας προσέφη [name]** (4.30): a common Homeric reply-formula ("greatly vexed, he
  addressed him"), rendered here "Him then, greatly vexed, addressed fair-haired Menelaus" / "Then,
  greatly troubled, fair-haired Menelaus said to him". It is very likely to recur in later books and
  should be formalized in the house table the first time it repeats.
- **τηλύγετος** (4.11, of Megapenthes): rendered "late-born", with the note stating plainly that the
  word's meaning is disputed (the alternative "tenderly loved, darling" is also argued, and neither
  etymology is secure). Not logged as a formula since it is a single adjective, not a recurring
  epithet pair in this part, but the disputed-meaning flag should carry forward if it recurs.
- **κητώεσσαν** (of Lacedaemon, 4.1): rendered "full-of-ravines", with the note flagging that the
  usual gloss ('full of hollows, ravines', from a noun κῆτος 'cavity') is not certain, and that the
  ancients sometimes connected the word with the homonymous κῆτος 'sea-monster'.
- **Ἐρεμβοί** (4.84): a people whose identity the ancients themselves disputed (Arabs, or a
  corruption of another ethnonym); the note says plainly that who they were is not known. Not a
  formula, just a proper name flagged as uncertain per the sole-source rule.
